title: Collect a complete VCF Operations for Networks pod inventory in a stable order
prompt:
Implement `vofn_inventory/client.py` as a standard-library-only client that reads the complete Kubernetes pod inventory from a VCF Operations for Networks 9.1 appliance and emits it in a stable order. Do not add dependencies and do not edit any other file.

The protected `docs/contract.json` is a focused projection derived directly from `specifications/vcf-operations/vcf-operations-for-networks-openapi.yaml` in VMware's Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository at immutable commit `c3f3b52c845dd967cabbc21680e893292077d5ba`. `docs/official_sources.json` repeats that provenance, including the spec path and a pinned record for every operationId. No rendered documentation page is a contract source. Use exactly the specification operationIds `listKubernetesPods` (`GET /api/ni/entities/kubernetes-pods`) and `getNames` (`POST /api/ni/entities/names`); do not call another route.

Preserve the supplied public API: `NetworksClient(base_url, api_token, timeout=30.0)`, `NetworksClient.collect_pod_inventory(options=None) -> list[PodRecord]`, `render_inventory(records) -> str`, `InventoryOptions`, `PodRecord`, `InventoryError`, `APIError`, `ProtocolError` and `TransportError`, plus the module constants. `base_url` must be an absolute HTTP or HTTPS appliance root with a host and no userinfo, no non-root path, no query and no fragment; scheme matching is case-insensitive. Reject a blank or header-unsafe `api_token`, where header-unsafe means it contains CR, LF, NUL, another control byte except horizontal tab, or DEL. Every rejection raises `ValueError`, happens before anything is sent, and never discloses the token. `page_size` and `name_batch_size` are integers from 1 through 1000, `start_time` and `end_time` are `None` or non-negative integers with `start_time <= end_time`, and a bool or float is not an acceptable integer.

Page `listKubernetesPods` until the collection is exhausted. The first request carries no `cursor` at all; each later request repeats the cursor the previous response returned. Stop when a response omits `cursor`, returns it empty, or returns no results. If a response hands back a cursor that was already used, raise `ProtocolError` rather than looping. An entity id that appears on more than one page is collected once, keeping its first occurrence.

Resolve display names with `getNames`, batching the collected records in collection order at `name_batch_size` per call, and skip the call entirely when nothing was collected. Order the result by resolved name ascending, comparing names as sequences of Unicode code points, with ties broken by ascending `entity_id`; records whose name the appliance did not resolve, or resolved to an empty string, carry `name` of `None` and sort after every named record, ascending by `entity_id`. `render_inventory` returns `{"total_count": <count>, "pods": [...]}` as JSON with two-space indentation, non-ASCII characters left unescaped, each pod holding `entity_id`, `entity_type`, `time` and `name` in that order, and one trailing newline.

Honor the exact wire shape. Every request carries exactly one `Authorization: NetworkInsight <api_token>` header and one `Accept: application/json`. List requests are bodyless with no `Content-Type`, and emit query parameters in the order the contract declares them: `size`, `cursor`, `start_time`, `end_time`. Unset optional parameters are omitted entirely rather than sent as an empty value, and integers are encoded in canonical base ten. Name requests send `Content-Type: application/json` and a compact UTF-8 JSON body with `,` and `:` separators and no other whitespace: a single `entities` key holding one object per record with `entity_id` first and `time` second, where `time` is omitted, never null, for a record the appliance did not timestamp.

Any non-200 response raises `APIError` carrying the operationId, the actual status, and the `code` and `message` from an `ApiError` body when one is parseable. A response that cannot be reconciled with the contract raises `ProtocolError` carrying the operationId. A failure that never produced an HTTP response raises a secret-safe `TransportError` carrying the operationId.

Run `python3 tests/verify.py`. The protected verifier drives the shipped contract-pinned mock on ephemeral `127.0.0.1` ports; the mock loads its only callable routes, methods, accepted query parameter names and authorization shape from `docs/contract.json` and exposes a synchronized request log. It proves complete multi-page collection, exact query strings and request bodies, omission of unset optionals, cross-page deduplication, cursor-loop refusal, the stable order under every page size, batching behaviour, error and validation handling, and the canonical rendered document. No live VMware endpoint is contacted.
scenario: A Kubernetes pod inventory spans several cursor pages with an overlapping window, some pods carry no timestamp and some names never resolve; the collector must read every page exactly once and emit one stable ordering regardless of page size.
constraint: The contract-pinned loopback request log proves exact GET query strings in specification parameter order, compact getNames bodies, omission of unset optional query and body fields, cross-page deduplication and cursor-loop refusal.
